extracted.intended_audience: Senior Area Chairs (SACs) for ICML 2025 / program committee members overseeing Area Chairs
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and expectations for Senior Area Chairs (SACs) overseeing Area Chairs (ACs) and the reviewing process for ICML 2025, including timelines, responsibilities for reviewer assignment and calibration, conflict-of-interest and confidentiality rules, and decision-finalization procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC core responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: As an SAC, your role is to oversee the work of a small number of ACs, making sure that the reviewing process goes smoothly. SACs serve as the first point of contact for ACs if they need assistance or guidance. SACs are responsible for helping ACs chase late reviewers, calibrating decisions across ACs, and discussing borderline papers. During the final decision-making phase, SACs discuss the proposed decisions with the program chairs (PCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be the primary supervisor for assigned ACs: provide guidance, chase late reviewers, help with calibration, lead discussions of borderline cases, and liaise with PCs for final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accurate contact/OpenReview profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure that your preferred email address is accurate in your OpenReview profile. We will send most emails from OpenReview (i.e., noreply@openreview.net). Such emails are sometimes accidentally marked as spam. Please check your spam folder regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitelist noreply@openreview.net, keep OpenReview profile up to date so you are assigned relevant ACs, and check spam folders to avoid missing time-sensitive messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by code of conduct and COI rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the ICML code of conduct. Read what constitutes conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with the Code of Conduct and conflict-of-interest definitions and apply them when overseeing ACs and discussions; contact PCs for COI questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review AC assignments and flag serious concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be assigned ~8 ACs to work with. Please review your assigned ACs and alert the PCs early of any potential serious concerns (e.g., ACs that are completely unqualified, any suspicious profiles/activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect AC qualifications and profiles promptly (by the AC assignment checking deadline) and escalate unqualified or suspicious ACs to the program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewer assignment quality and adherence to limits
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will be checking and possibly modifying reviewer assignments during February 7-11. Make sure that each AC you work with has four qualified reviewers for each paper they are handling. We are allowing ACs to make at most two changes to the initial reviewer assignment for each paper they are handling (i.e., swap out at most two reviewers). If an AC wants to make more than two changes, or if they want to invite an external reviewer, they will need you to do it for them (with your approval, of course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help ACs find qualified reviewers not in conflict with the paper. If additional changes or external reviewers are needed, approve and perform them through OpenReview (do not share submissions outside OpenReview).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure each paper has at least 3 high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the author response period starts, ensure that all of the papers your ACs are assigned have at least 3 high quality reviews. Make sure that ACs check for any disrespectful or derogatory language in the reviews. You are ultimately responsible for making sure the reviews are all there and high quality, so if an AC is unresponsive you will need to step in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor reviewer completion during the review window and step in to chase missing or low-quality reviews; enforce respectful tone and remediate unprofessional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage emergency review period and external reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If any reviews are still missing, it is urgent to help your ACs track them down or invite additional reviewers. ACs may ask you to invite external reviewers on their behalf, but please do this through OpenReview directly rather than sharing submissions through other channels like email. ACs are asked to keep the total number of reviewers per paper to at most 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the emergency review window (March 14–24), actively assist in recruiting reviewers, invite externals via OpenReview, and enforce the reviewer-count cap. Note updated policy: ACs can invite external reviewers themselves as of March 17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage author response and discussion period
rubrics_metrics.description: This year, we are limiting the number of communication rounds between reviewers and authors. Furthermore, ACs should be checking that reviewers acknowledge the Author response by April 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviewers engage with/acknowledge author responses within the stated deadline and that discussion rounds adhere to the conference’s limits; use provided detailed instructions for author-reviewer discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure AC-Reviewer discussions are initiated and active
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs should lead a discussion via OpenReview for each submission and make sure the reviewers engage in the discussion phase as needed. If your assigned ACs have not initiated discussions, prompt them to do so, especially for the papers where there are positive and negative reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt ACs to start and moderate discussions, especially when reviewer opinions conflict; verify meaningful reviewer engagement during the April 1–13 window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely preliminary meta-reviews and AC calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Remind ACs to submit preliminary meta-reviews for each paper, and begin to schedule one-on-one discussions with them for the next phase. Consider organizing meetings between pairs or groups of ACs so that they have the chance to talk over their decisions and better calibrate; you may choose to be present for these meetings or ask that ACs meet with each other before discussing papers with you. Check carefully for COIs before asking ACs to discuss papers with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure preliminary meta-reviews are submitted by the meta-review deadline (April 14), organize calibration meetings, and confirm COI checks when grouping ACs for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate decisions, focus on borderline and conflicting cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Help calibrate decisions by working closely with your ACs. Schedule meetings with them individually and/or in groups. Pay particularly close attention to borderline papers and papers in which the AC’s recommendation goes against the recommendations of the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read all reviews for papers assigned to ACs when you feel guidance is needed; prioritize borderline/conflict cases and use calibration meetings to align standards across ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review quality and explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Read all meta-reviews. Make sure they explain paper decisions to the authors. Meta-reviews should augment the reviews, and explain how the reviews, author responses, and discussion were used to arrive at the decision. Dismissing or ignoring a review is not acceptable unless there is a good reason for doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure meta-reviews justify decisions clearly, reference reviews and responses, and do not arbitrarily ignore reviews; require ACs to revise weak meta-reviews before notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with Program Chairs to finalize decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to discuss all borderline papers and cases in which the recommendation of the AC goes against the recommendations of the reviewers. Update meta-reviews to accurately reflect the final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the SAC-PC discussion period (April 21–25), present borderline cases, follow PC guidance, and revise meta-reviews to match the final decisions before notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality and rules on submission use/sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep everything relating to the review process confidential. Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they become publicly available. Do not talk about or distribute submissions (whether it is the code, or the ideas and results described in them) to anyone without prior approval from the program chairs. Code submitted for reviewing cannot be distributed. If you wish to invite an external reviewer, do so through OpenReview rather than sharing submissions through another channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never distribute submissions or incorporate unpublished ideas/code into your research; use only OpenReview channels for inviting externals; seek PC approval for any exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactively monitor AC responsiveness and process health
rubrics_metrics.description: It is your responsibility to ensure that the review process goes smoothly. Check in to make sure that the ACs you work with are responsive, help them find emergency reviewers, and make sure discussion is happening on their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly check AC activity during critical windows, follow up on stalled tasks, and step in when an AC is unresponsive to keep timelines on track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be responsive and respect deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Be responsive. Respect deadlines and respond to emails as promptly as possible. If you will be unavailable (e.g., on vacation) for more than a few days—especially during important windows (e.g., decision-making)—please let the program chairs know as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain timely communication with ACs and PCs, and notify PCs of planned absences so coverage can be arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be kind and flexible when handling late or incomplete work
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to acknowledge that personal situations may lead to late or unfinished work among reviewers and ACs. In the event that a reviewer or an AC is unable to complete their work on time, we encourage you to be considerate of the personal circumstances; you might have to pick up the slack in some cases. If necessary, make a back-up plan with another reviewer or AC, and be flexible to the extent possible. In all communications, exhibit empathy and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show empathy, arrange backup plans (e.g., reassign tasks), and balance firmness on deadlines with human considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalate conflicts of interest and restrict cross-SAC/AC discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the reviewing process is double blind at the level of ACs, it is your responsibility to be on the lookout for uncaught conflicts of interest. If you notice a conflict of interest with a submission that is assigned to one of your ACs, contact program chairs right away. Do not talk to other SACs about submissions assigned to your ACs without prior approval from program chairs since other SACs may have conflicts with these submissions. Do not talk to other SACs or ACs about submissions you are an author on or submissions with which you have a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly report suspected COIs to PCs, avoid cross-SAC/AC discussions on assigned submissions without PC approval, and recuse yourself from discussing submissions you have a COI with.
